paper_analogy: Deep Reinforcement Learning on Graphs for Autonomous Search-and-Track
source: test_data.csv, Machine == 'pilgrimage', 15 row(s), 1 auto-detected run(s)/playthroughs. Graph built directly from the PTT (Penetration Testing Tree) field's growth.

analogy_mapping.Agent Nodes: PTT snapshot reached after each new tree item (state = cumulative tree)
analogy_mapping.Search Nodes: The PTT tree item worked on (number + title) + its MCP_tasks tool calls
analogy_mapping.Track Nodes: That item's findings payload -- what was actually discovered

node_types.Agent (Blue/Pink goal): PTT state after a new item completes
node_types.Search (Orange): PTT item being worked (tool calls in tooltip)

edge_types.StateTransition (Black): Agent -> Agent, label = PTT item number
edge_types.SearchUpdate (Green): Agent -> Search, item being worked from that state
edge_types.TrackUpdate (Blue): Search -> Track, what item's execution found
edge_types.Prediction (Purple): Track -> Agent, leads to next cumulative PTT state

nodes.title:
1.15 Do a vulnerability analysis on the Binwalk v2.3.2:
The version of Binwalk being used, v2.3.2, is known to have several security vulnerabilities. The most severe vulnerability, CVE-2022-4510, is a path traversal flaw leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE). This is located in the Professional File System (PFS) extractor plugin. By crafting a malicious PFS filesystem file, an attacker can force Binwalk to extract files to arbitrary locations outside the intended extraction directory. Binwalk versions from 2.1.2b through 2.3.3 are vulnerable to this. The recommended mitigation is to upgrade Binwalk to version 2.3.4 or later. Another vulnerability, CVE-2021-4287, exists in Binwalk versions up to 2.3.2. It involves a symlink
